acceptanceCriteria.text: Both token methods have a PowerShell block next to the POSIX block.
The token-file example restricts the file to the current user and writes no newline or BOM.
Both examples were run once in PowerShell 5.1 against a scratch project and succeeded (output in the submission).

body:
docs/runbooks/cli.md:104-107 (token file) and :111-114 (export DM_SESSION_TOKEN) are POSIX only, while the attachments section already pairs PowerShell with Git Bash (:57-77).

## Do
In docs/runbooks/cli.md:
1. Label each existing sh block "POSIX shells (bash, zsh, Git Bash):".
2. After the block at 104-107 add "PowerShell:" and a powershell block:
   $tokenFile = Join-Path $HOME '.dm-token'
   Set-Content -NoNewline -Encoding ascii -Path $tokenFile -Value 'dmg_…'
   icacls $tokenFile /inheritance:r /grant:r "${env:USERNAME}:(R,W)" | Out-Null
   node out/main/cli.js --token-file $tokenFile call list_epics
3. After the block at 111-114 add "In PowerShell (for this session only; Remove-Item Env:DM_SESSION_TOKEN clears it):" and a powershell block:
   $env:DM_SESSION_TOKEN = 'dmg_…'
   node out/main/cli.js call list_epics
Use list_epics because it needs no JSON (line 35 explains why inline JSON breaks in PowerShell).

## Out of scope
cmd.exe; CLI help text (src/cli/args.ts:52-56); the Linear section.

## Tests
Docs only. Run both PowerShell examples once in Windows PowerShell 5.1 against a CLI built from this branch and a scratch project under the system temp folder with its own grant (never this repository's live project), and paste the output into the submission.

## Rules
This card is the complete fix: nothing it finds is left for a later card. Fix anything that blocks a criterion inside this card. Run the listed tests, `npm run typecheck`, and `npx oxlint` on the touched files.
title: Add PowerShell token syntax to the CLI runbook
